assessment.nobel_worthiness: The collateral-constraint framework transformed macroeconomic accounts of amplification, credit cycles, and real-financial linkages.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore supplied the seminal dynamic mechanism; later financial-accelerator work broadened and operationalized it.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism has been deeply incorporated into macro-finance theory and tested against repeated credit-boom and crisis episodes.
uncertainties: The candidate package encompasses several distinct extensions, making the precise boundary of the credited discovery important.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made resource misallocation a central quantitative explanation for large productivity and income differences across countries.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Restuccia, and Klenow are closely associated with the measurement, theory, and cross-country application of the misallocation agenda.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a large subsequent literature on firms, development, policy distortions, and aggregate productivity.
uncertainties: Measured wedges are reduced-form objects, so their causal interpretation and policy mapping remain contested.
The broad literature has important intellectual precursors and contributors beyond the proposed trio.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian synthesis supplied the modern analytical framework for monetary policy, unifying nominal rigidities, welfare analysis, and stabilization policy.
assessment.attribution: Calvo's tractable pricing formulation and the contributions of Woodford and Gali to the framework and policy analysis are especially central.
assessment.maturity: The approach has shaped central-bank models, academic macroeconomics, and empirical monetary-policy analysis for decades.
uncertainties: The listed discovery is unusually broad, with many indispensable contributors and an attribution problem under the three-laureate limit.
Its empirical adequacy in environments with nonlinearities and financial frictions remains debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection fundamentally changed trade theory's account of aggregate trade gains, productivity, and distributional consequences.
assessment.attribution: Melitz's model is the focal foundational contribution, while Helpman and Redding made major related theoretical and empirical advances.
assessment.maturity: The framework is standard in international-trade research and has been extensively developed, estimated, and applied.
uncertainties: The appropriate attribution between the seminal model and the wider heterogeneous-firm trade program needs careful delineation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification redirected empirical economics toward conclusions that remain credible when point identification rests on implausibly strong assumptions.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the foundational intellectual figure; Tamer and Molinari made substantial contributions to moment-inequality methods and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature, broadly used across applied fields, and has permanently altered standards for transparent identification.
uncertainties: The candidate combines a foundational conceptual contribution with a broad set of later econometric methods.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental evidence and theory on reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion altered economic models of incentives, contracting, and social interaction.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Falk are leading architects of the experimental and behavioral program; Schmidt's theoretical contribution is central to inequity-aversion modeling.
assessment.maturity: The findings have been replicated, extensively applied, and integrated into behavioral and personnel economics.
uncertainties: The scope and external validity of laboratory evidence, and the attribution of the wider social-preferences literature, remain debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Axiomatic models of ambiguity supplied rigorous alternatives to subjective expected utility and reshaped analysis of decisions under model uncertainty.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa's maxmin expected-utility work and Epstein's recursive treatment of ambiguity are foundational; Marinacci is a major contributor to the broader field.
assessment.maturity: The theories have had durable influence in decision theory, finance, macroeconomics, and mechanism design.
uncertainties: Empirical discrimination among ambiguity models and their quantitative importance are less settled than their theoretical influence.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of top income, wealth, and offshore holdings made distributional measurement central to contemporary research and policy debate.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez, and Zucman have provided defining data, methods, and interpretive work for the modern long-run inequality agenda.
assessment.maturity: The research has produced influential international data infrastructure and a vast follow-on literature.
uncertainties: Tax-record and wealth-capitalization methods require consequential assumptions and vary in comparability across countries and periods.
The strength of causal claims and policy implications exceeds what descriptive measurement alone can establish.
